cells.tense: You are holding a long finish together, and the last stretch has come into view.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Take the last stretch a piece at a time, on your own reserves, slow days included. When a piece is done and the pull says grip harder, loosen instead. Stop there.
cells.core:
You can hold on past the point where it stops being comfortable, and lately that hold is what carries this finish. The hope didn't run out; you kept going, and the end has come into view. Keeping hold without forcing means letting the grip ease after a long carry — firm while the weight is on you, looser the moment it isn't.

Take the last stretch a piece at a time, on your own reserves, slow days included. When a piece is done and the old pull says grip harder, loosen instead, and stop there for the day. You have proved enough already. What's left is bringing it in without pushing against the finish itself.
cells.sheetLine: You are finishing something the long way, and it holds.
cells.growth: Non-attachment (Intent — the willingness to release what has been carried)
cells.verb: Following through on a hope long past the point where hoping was easy
cells.place: At the close of something, where finishing and starting share the same room

cells.tense: You will keep reaching past this finish toward the next hard thing before this one is done.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Write down the almost-finished and the hardly-started, close the page, and let it sit for a day before you decide what either one means. No verdicts out loud.
cells.core:
This capacity at its best lets a thing finish in its own time: you can hold an unfinished piece without rehearsing its hard parts, and the not-knowing sits easily. The reach stays the size of the next real step, and the power lands on what is actually moving.

Right now the strength that carries you is outrunning the thing it carries. You rehearse the hard parts of a completion that hasn't happened, reaching into difficulty that has asked nothing of you, and the reach is larger than the finish. The push shows up in the planning before anything has moved.

Write down the almost-finished and the hardly-started, close the page, and let it sit for a day before you decide what either means. No verdicts out loud. The strength is real; it doesn't have to prove itself against a date that hasn't come.

cells.tense: You have been standing at a door that is already shut behind you, still carrying what it took to cross.
cells.ask: Give a week to what is already on your hands — dishes, a plant, a load of laundry. A few ordinary minutes a day, nothing grander. What can wait can wait.
cells.core:
The crossing happened and you are still at the threshold of it, carrying the weight of having gone through. Your hands know the motions, and they keep going. Nothing in you reads as aimed at anything while they do it — the engine turns over, and the key turned long before this.

Give a week to what is already on your hands — dishes, a plant, a load of laundry. A few ordinary minutes a day, nothing grander; what can wait can wait. Care that asks little of you is still care, and direction comes back to a hand in motion on real ground.

cells.tense: You are holding a long finish together while the account says it came together on its own.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: One evening at the plain middle of the work, nothing else open, no progress counted. Work, then stop. Leave the result where it sits.
cells.core:
You keep finishing things, and the story of how they get finished has them finishing themselves. The persistence runs through your hands, unnamed, and the telling leaves the effort out. When that effort gets left out of the account, someone still has to remember it happened.

One evening at the plain middle of the work, nothing else open, no progress counted. Work, then stop, and leave the result where it sits. That much is yours to see. What carries the finish doesn't need a speech; it needs to be held at the size it actually is, in your own account, at least once.
